title: smart-routing-fallback-debug-notes-ethan-park
content:
Goal: capture breadcrumbs + commands/errors for the smart-routing regional failover incident (Feb 18-24). Personal scratchpad - messy.

Summary (plain):
- User traffic hit elevated tail latency in eu-west-1 around 2026-02-18 09:15 UTC.
- Smart routing attempted regional failover to us-east-1 per policy, but many requests returned 503/502s or long queue times.
- Hypothesis: fallback policy routing to model-variant that isn't compatible with routing key (quantized path mismatch) + capacity spike on target pool, plus a config mismatch that made circuit-breaker thresholds too tight.

Timeline / observed signals:
- 2026-02-18 09:12 UTC: spikes in request latency for route /v1/generate (eu-west-1). Requests queued, many timed out on client (timeout ~ 15s).
- 09:14 UTC: smart-router logs show fallback decision to region us-east-1.
- 09:15-09:22 UTC: us-east-1 serving nodes reported a series of 502s from load balancer -> 503 upstream from runtime.
- 09:24 UTC: autoscaler triggered but scale-up slowed (insights: reserved pool constraints).
- 09:40 UTC: manual mitigation: changed fallback_policy to regional-prefer then forced local-retry disabled; partial recovery.

Commands tried (notes + outputs):
- Check router decision logs (ELK):
  curl -s "https://elk.example.internal/_search?q=router:fallback AND route:/v1/generate&size=50" | jq '.hits.hits[]._source | {ts: .timestamp, decision: .router_decision, target_region: .target_region}'
  --> saw many entries with target_region: "us-east-1", decision: "fallback_capacity_policy_v2"

- Inspect smart-router config at time of incident:
  kubectl -n infra get configmap smart-router-config -o yaml | sed -n '/fallback_policy/,/end/p'
  --> fallback_policy: "regional-first"
      fallback_variants:
        - name: small-quantized
          compatible_kernels: [f16, int8]
  Note: later saw an override on global config that set fallback_variants for eu-* differently (mismatch).

- Check serving-runtime logs for us-east-1 pool (tail):
  kubectl -n serving-runtime logs deployment/serve-us-east-gen --since=1h | grep -E "ERROR|WARN|503|502|kv cache miss" | tail -n 60
  ERROR: request handler failed: upstream_write: broken pipe
  WARN: local-kv-cache: eviction pressure high (70%)
  ERROR: model-variant small-quantized: kernel-load-failure: symbol not found: fast_attention_opt
  502 from lb: upstream returned 502 for /v1/generate

- Confirmed model artifact presence in us-east pool:
  ls -lh /mnt/models/model-x-v2/variants/small-quantized/  # returns files but kernel .so missing

- Check registry / model build job status:
  curl -s "https://registry.internal/api/models/model-x-v2/builds?status=failed" | jq '.'
  --> found a failed build on 2026-02-17 23:40 UTC for small-quantized (missing kernel due to build config change).

- Circuit breaker / limiter checks:
  redis-cli -h redis-router info | grep -i broken
  redis-cli HGETALL router:circuit_breakers:route:/v1/generate
  --> saw recent tripping counts: fallback_count=1243, cb_tripped=true, last_tripped_ts=2026-02-18T09:16:02Z

- Batching stats (from metrics):
  prometheus query: sum(rate(requests_total{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (region, pool)
  --> eu-west-1: 120r/s baseline -> spike to 800r/s
  --> us-east-1 (fallback pool): baseline 40r/s -> spike to 600r/s (exhausted concurrency)

Error snippets (copied):
- ERROR: model-variant small-quantized: kernel-load-failure: symbol not found: fast_attention_opt
- WARN: fallback decision but target pool capacity low, enqueueing to waiting-queue (len=512)
- ERROR upstream_write: broken pipe
- 503 Service Unavailable (upstream overloaded)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Model artifact mismatch: small-quantized builds missing optimized kernel (fast_attention_opt) for us-east, so runtime returns errors leading to LB 502/503. This combined with sudden traffic resulted in cascading failures.
2) Fallback policy allowed routing to incompatible variant (regional-first) without compatibility check enforcement, so router sent traffic to a variant that cannot serve certain request shapes.
3) Circuit-breaker thresholds are too aggressive for cross-region retries: cb tripped early and prevented progressive backoff, causing many clients to get immediate 5xx rather than retries to secondary pools.
4) Autoscaler reserve limits / quotas prevented fast scale-up of fallback pool; reserved capacity pre-allocated incorrectly.

Evidence supporting #1 & #2:
- build failure in model registry for small-quantized on 2026-02-17 (missed kernel).
- runtime logs show kernel-load-failure on small-quantized variant in us-east.
- router config had fallback_variants listing small-quantized for eu -> us failover path.

Quick mitigation steps we performed (notes):
- 09:26 UTC: disabled fallback to small-quantized by updating smart-router configmap and reloading (kubectl apply + curl reload endpoint). Partial stop of 502s.
- 09:30 UTC: temporarily increased circuit-breaker thresholds to allow slow drain (redis HSET router:cb:... tripping_threshold 200).
- 09:42 UTC: roll-forward: reverted to local-region-only routing while we repaired the model build.

Permanent fixes proposed (items for follow-up):
- Enforce variant compatibility checks in router: before routing to variant X, ensure runtime reports variant as healthy+kernel-supported for the requested model shape. (owner: eng-serving-runtime)
- Add a pre-deploy validation in model registry to ensure kernel artifact present for all target architectures/regions. (owner: applied-ml + release-eng)
- Relax circuit-breaker to allow slow failover with exponential backoff, and add a secondary retry policy to attempt alternative pools only after backlog below threshold. (owner: eng-sre + router team)
- Autoscaler policy: allow pre-burst headroom for fallback pools for cross-region failover windows; sanity check reserved quotas. (owner: infra + dedicated)
- Postmortem: link incident timeline, metrics, config diffs, and the build failure (INC-2026-0421).

Notes for debugging next time (quick checklist):
- Check model-registry build status for any variant referenced by fallback map.
- Confirm kernel .so presence and checksum on each region / pool.
- Query router decision logs for target_variant and compatibility flags.
- Check CB/trips in redis for route-level settings before toggling global thresholds.
- If LB returns 502/503 in fallback pool, verify runtime logs for kernel failures (this is high-signal).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Why did the small-quantized build fail on 2026-02-17? (build logs show missing compile flag; need release-eng follow-up).
- Should fallback policy be changed to prefer model-compatibility over region? (tradeoffs: latency vs reliability).
- Add synthetic canary flows that validate full end-to-end path (router->runtime->kernel) for each new variant.

References (internal):
- Incident ticket: INC-2026-0421
- Jira: PROD-8123 (model build fix)
- Confluence: serving-runtime/fallback-playbook (draft)

Raw notes: (quick paste)
- "if kernel missing -> runtime returns 500 and LB surfaces 502/503; routing still thinks pool healthy because healthcheck only checks process up not kernel symbol presence"
- "we should add a variant-level healthcheck: runtime exposes /health/variant/<name> that checks kernel symbols and model load success"

Next steps (my personal):
- Pair with Marcus on the build fix (today).
- Add router guard: check runtime variant-health endpoint before routing (spike + PR).
- Draft postmortem skeleton and send to incident channel.

-- Ethan
(scratchpad, do not publish as-is)
